clue.text: Scientist who is reportedly an authority on the expiration dates of consumer products?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the clue is asking for a sound

parts.words: an authority on the expiration dates of consumer products
parts.note: a 'sell-by' date is when a product expires, and an -ologist is an expert

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about which kind of scientist would be the expert on when groceries go off.
explanation.walkthrough: CELL BIOLOGIST said aloud is 'sell-by-ologist': someone who studies sell-by dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell biologist is a researcher in the life sciences who studies cells.

clue.text: Reinterpret Jung, probing one source of heat in a marriage

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: coal is a fuel burned for heat

indicators.note: to reinterpret something is to recast it differently, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A psychoanalytic reading of Carl Jung applied to what keeps a marriage passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugal means relating to marriage or to the relationship between spouses.

clue.text: Fat lip: one delivered on the face

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
d. is a commercial abbreviation for delivered
surface padding that completes the picture of a punch

explanation.surface: A swollen lip, the kind you get from a punch landed on your face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat lip' reads as one phrase, but 'Fat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the class of biological compounds that includes fats and oils.

clue.text: College degree and clean representation — that's money in the bank

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: a representation shows something in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A degree and a spotless image are said to be as good as savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance is the amount of money held in a bank account.

clue.text: Eject American in overtime

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: OT is the usual abbreviation for overtime
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A sports scene: an American player thrown out of the game in extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to force them out, which is what ejecting does.

clue.text: Wipe out, having basic knowledge of childbirth

parts.note: OB, short for obstetrics, is the branch of medicine dealing with childbirth
being able to read and write is having basic knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone who knows the basics of giving birth decides to erase everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A of B' puts B first here: the childbirth word comes before the knowledge word.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate something is to destroy it completely, leaving no trace.

clue.text: Entrance French painter with onset of surrealism

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter

indicators.note: the onset is the very beginning, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the art movement's name

explanation.surface: A French artist dabbling in surrealism is enchanting, as if entrancing a gallery visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads like the verb to enchant, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for the act or means of entering, a way in.

clue.text: Use force to separate drink, criticism and creative activity

parts.note: tea is a drink
a rap is a rebuke or criticism
art is creative activity

explanation.surface: Someone forcibly prying apart their tea, critics and creative pursuits.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear apart is to rip something into pieces by force.

clue.text: Border inside reunited Germany

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the following words

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A frontier within Germany after East and West were reunited in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the boundary or rim of something, a synonym for border.

clue.text: Trained spaniel for Tenzing Norgay et al.

indicators.note: training puts something through drills that reshape it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog has been trained to accompany the Sherpa who climbed Everest with Hillary.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenzing Norgay, the Sherpa who reached Everest's summit with Edmund Hillary in 1953, was from Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenzing and his fellow countrymen are people of Nepal, hence plural natives of that Himalayan country.

clue.text: Slowpoke to pull young woman back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the assembled words from the end towards the start

parts.note: to pull is to drag
gal is informal for a young woman

explanation.surface: Someone slow is told to haul a girl back, as if lagging behind on a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowpoke is someone who dawdles and falls behind, which is exactly what a laggard does.

clue.text: Incomplete, no nude is offensive

indicators.note: an offensive is a violent attack, and these letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prudish verdict that a half-finished picture without any nudity is still objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Work left undone is unfinished, so the word is a synonym for incomplete.

clue.text: Herb stows mangled tree in poor quarters aboard ship

indicators.note: to stow something is to pack it away inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb

indicators.note: something mangled is twisted out of shape, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb packs a damaged tree into the cheap cabins of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name, but it is the plant sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger accommodation on a ship, for those paying the lowest fares.

clue.text: When mentioning the Nutmeg State, don't pronounce the first syllable and DON'T SHOUT LIKE THIS, for instance

definitions.text: DON'T SHOUT LIKE THIS, for instance

indicators.note: leaving the first syllable unspoken cuts the opening sound off the state's name
mentioning is speaking, so what counts is how the remaining word sounds

parts.note: the Nutmeg State is the nickname of Connecticut, said here without its opening 'Con'

explanation.surface: A style guide's instructions on saying a state's name, ending with a reminder not to use capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Connecticut minus its first syllable sounds like NETIQUETTE. Writing in all capitals online reads as shouting, so 'don't shout like this' is a classic example of the online etiquette rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Netiquette is the set of polite conventions for online communication, such as avoiding all-caps text.

clue.text: Try starting late — that's more than sufficient

explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, a quantity beyond what is merely enough.

clue.text: Limps to an unusually classical view of the world

indicators.note: unusually means in an unexpected way, so the letters appear in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles towards an unconventional ancient philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonism is the philosophy of Plato, an ancient Greek outlook based on ideal forms.

clue.text: Early Italian's genuine back-to front examination

indicators.note: the back of the word is brought round to its front, so its last letter moves to the start

parts.note: genuine means true
a scan is a close examination

explanation.surface: An ancient Italian's authentic medical examination, done in some topsy-turvy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to front' is not a full reversal: only the final letter of the word for genuine moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were the people of ancient Etruria, in central Italy before Rome rose to power.

clue.text: Knight quietly mounting to get involved in concrete act of vengeance

indicators.note: getting involved in something means going into it, so these letters go inside another word

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act, revenge taken against someone for a wrong.

clue.text: Prohibit support for Pete Seeger, e.g.

a joist is a supporting beam

explanation.surface: A call to stop backing the folk singer, as in the blacklisting days of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: Pete Seeger, the American folk singer blacklisted in the McCarthy era, played the five-string banjo.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeger was a famous banjo player, an example of the musician the answer names.

clue.text: Prize cheese casserole

parts.note: Monterey Jack is an American cheese
a pot is a casserole dish

explanation.surface: A cheese casserole that has won a prize, like a recipe at a county fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like an adjective for the casserole, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the large top prize in a lottery or game of chance.

clue.text: Not very bright time to interrupt spouse

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another thing

parts.note: a mate is a partner or spouse
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dim moment for someone who keeps cutting off their husband or wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very bright' suggests a dull person, but here it describes a non-shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte finish is dull rather than glossy, so it is not very bright.

clue.text: On Wall Street, option 9: I'm rising to fight

indicators.note: rising means going up, so in a down answer the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a put is a stock option to sell at a set price
IX is 9 in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stock trader announces that option number nine is climbing, ready to do battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run of pieces, not just I'm, is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix it up is an informal idiom meaning to brawl or get into a fight.

clue.text: Reading group's bad luck: being held hostage by an idiot

clue.text: Has-been's half-crazy party

explanation.definitionFit: A bash is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Announce someone leaving English city

explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is the county town of Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Surreptitiously steal electric car

clue.text: Musicians, perhaps from Dire Straits

clue.text: Hester Prynne's nacre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the heroine of Hawthorne's The Scarlet Letter, whose daughter is named Pearl
second meaning: the iridescent lining of some shells

explanation.walkthrough: In The Scarlet Letter, Hester Prynne's child is Pearl, so she is literally the mother of Pearl; the possessive 's joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the lustrous substance lining oyster shells, also called mother-of-pearl, and Hester is the parent of a girl named Pearl.
